title: Story of the Kazi and His Slipper

keywords: story of the kazi and his slipper
full_text:
In Baghdad lived a wealthy but notorious miser named Abu Kasim, who possessed a pair of ancient, wretched slippers. For twenty years he had patched them with bits of old leather, copper rivets, and coarse twine, until they weighed as much as stone blocks and were known to every resident as the ugliest shoes in Islam.

One day, Abu Kasim visited the public baths. While he was bathing, an honorable Kazi came to bathe as well, leaving his brand-new yellow morocco leather slippers by the dressing benches.
When Abu Kasim finished, he looked for his footwear, but someone had moved his wretched slippers. Seeing the elegant yellow slippers, the miser chuckled: 'Ah! Some friend has left me a gift!' He slipped them on and walked home.

When the Kazi emerged and found only Abu Kasim's infamous patched clogs, he flew into a rage, had the miser arrested, and fined him a heavy sum of thirty dinars.

Humiliated, Abu Kasim returned home and angrily threw his old slippers out of the window into the Tigris river.
Three days later, a fisherman casting his net dragged up the heavy slippers. The sharp iron rivets tore the net to shreds. Enraged, the fisherman ran to Abu Kasim's house and hurled the wet slippers through the window!
The heavy shoes struck a row of expensive crystal rosewater flasks that Abu Kasim had purchased for resale, shattering them all!

Abu Kasim wept: 'Accursed slippers!'
He took a spade, carried the shoes into his garden in the dead of night, and began digging a deep pit to bury them.
A neighbor, seeing him dig in the dark, reported to the watch that Abu Kasim had found a buried treasure without declaring it to the treasury!
The police arrested him, and the Governor fined him another hundred dinars before releasing him!

Desperate, Abu Kasim carried the slippers far outside the city and threw them into a mountain aqueduct.
The bulky shoes lodged in the sluice gate, blocking the water supply to the royal gardens and drowning the Sultan's prize tulip beds!
Once again, Abu Kasim was identified by his famous slippers and fined five hundred dinars!

Exasperated to the brink of madness, Abu Kasim picked up the soaked, mud-caked slippers, walked straight into the Grand Kazi's hall, slammed them onto the judge's table, and shouted:
'My Lord! Behold the cause of all my ruin! I beg thee, draw up a solemn legal decree declaring that these slippers are divorced from me, that I am no longer their owner, and that whatever disaster they commit henceforth—be it flood, fire, or earthquake—Abu Kasim is not responsible!'

The entire court erupted in laughter. The Kazi pardoned him on condition that he cast the accursed shoes into the public furnace and buy a clean, modest pair of shoes, teaching the old miser that false economy and stubborn clinging to old junk cost far more than honest generosity.
moral: Clinging stubbornly to worn-out possessions out of avarice brings endless trouble; let go of what is past.
